evidence: Parsed every judge.toml with tomllib. Gates: render hro_gate_render and constraints hro_gate_shared are both type=binary (scoring.toml [gates] render=0.0, constraints=0.0), which fits all-or-nothing preconditions. Functional: all 44 criteria are type=binary with positive weights 0.5-2.5; every description is a pass/fail behavioural assertion ending 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold' (e.g. functional/judge.toml:47 duplicate-email refusal, :56 one-stage moves, :272 activity lines, :344 unread counts). The only quality-sounding words ('readable line' at :272, 'readable content' in gates/render/judge.toml:23) are factual presence checks, not degree-of-craft. Polish: all 5 criteria binary (live_board, live_thread, earlier_place, failed_send, session_resume); each is a concrete state-preservation behaviour with explicit pass/fail conditions (draft text unchanged, document.activeElement retained, scroll not reset, getBoundingClientRect().top within a few pixels, sent once), so binary is the correct type and matches the template's binary polish. Visual: all 5 criteria (hro_vis_type, _color, _layout, _hierarchy, _consistency) are type=likert, points=5, weight 1.2, each with five described anchors 5..1 (visual/judge.toml:24-29, 39-44, 54-59, 69-74, 84-89); these are the craft/degree-of-quality items. Anchors 1..5 match RewardKit Likert.normalize ((raw-1)/(points-1)) and visual/prompt.md:7,12,16 which map gate failure / unobserved to raw Likert 1 (normalized zero) and say 'grade every criterion independently with its five anchors'. (The template's visual anchors additionally list a 0 level outside the 1..5 scale; the task's 1..5 set is cleaner, not a defect.) Per SKILL.md:65 and quality-checks.md:170 the internal 'we don't use Likert' note is a known false positive; judged against the shipped format there are no binary craft criteria and no likert block without anchors. Attempted counterexamples: (a) broken app passing via type mismatch - a visually crude but functional app cannot get full visual credit because craft is graded on 1-5 anchors rather than a lenient binary; a dead app is zeroed by the visual gate (prompt.md:11-12). (b) conforming alternative failing - polish binaries describe observable behaviour, not a house style; a conforming app with different styling is not penalised there, and visual anchors are style-agnostic ('Layout, labels and styles are the implementer's choice', prompt.md:14). No type-fit defect found. This is a static rubric-design assessment; it does not assert any judge run outcome, Oracle or model score.
